title: Anchorline Summit - Night Watch Summary and Follow-ups
body:
Night-watch summary (2027-08-25 23:00 - 2027-08-26 07:00 UTC)

1) Incident snapshot - KV-cache thrash (incident SRE-4321)
- Window: 2027-08-26 01:12 - 2027-08-26 02:03 UTC
- Symptom: sudden increase in per-token latency for hosted-api tokenization path; tail p95 jumped from 85ms to ~420ms across a subset of requests.
- Root cause hypothesis: KV cache eviction loop triggered on a new model variant (gptx-v1-q) causing repeated cache fills + synchronous persistence calls to the metadata store.
- Immediate mitigations applied: rolled back routing policy to gptx-v1-q-fallback (2027-08-26 01:24 UTC), temporarily raised cache-size threshold on affected pool, and disabled the persistence flush in the runtime patch.
- Current state: degraded -> recovered; routing remains pinned to fallback variant pending follow-ups.

2) Escalations and owners
- Pager: Diego Marquez (primary) responded 01:14 UTC and coordinated rollback.
- On-call eng: Asha Patel (you) performed the cache threshold bump and stabilization checks.
- Runtime infra owner: Lina Zhou to investigate persistent write path and quantify I/O pattern (action item).
- Product/Model onboarding: Rajesh Nair to check canary config that promoted gptx-v1-q into low-latency path.

3) Runbook gaps discovered (draft notes)
- Current runbook 'kv-cache-thrash' assumes eviction is memory-only; we observed metadata persistence creating I/O amplification. Add steps to:
  * identify persistence enabled models via /admin/model-configs
  * command to temporarily toggle persistence: infra-cli model update --id <model> --persistence=off
  * clear indicators for immediate rollback vs. canary-pause.
- Missing automated alert: create alert for 'cache eviction rate' > 500/min per pool.
- Add checklist for routing pin + rollback and for coordinated announcement to hosting teams.

4) Follow-ups (tickets + timelines)
- SRE-4321 (root cause analysis): owner Lina Zhou, due 2027-09-02.
- OPS-1147 (runbook update + new alert): owner Asha Patel, due 2027-08-30.
- INFRA-618 (runtime patch to make persistence async-safe): PR open (linked), owner Rajesh, due 2027-09-06.

5) Actions taken during shift (chronological)
- 00:58 UTC: noticed upward trend in p95 via dashboard; opened brief incident doc and pinged #sre-ops.
- 01:05 UTC: replicated latency locally via synthetic; confirmed correlation with model variant.
- 01:14 UTC: Diego paged and suggested rollback routing; rolled back 01:24 UTC.
- 01:36 UTC: raised cache-size threshold + disabled persistence flush; observed p95 drop to ~95ms by 01:50 UTC.

6) Checks completed before handoff
- Dashboard health: all green except 'kv-eviction-rate' metric now at nominal.
- Open alerts: SRE-4321 (resolved, monitor for 24h).
- Consumer impact: no customer-facing 5xx spike detected; minor latency blips for a subset of low-priority requests.
- Canary status: canary pool currently disabled for gptx-v1-q until infra patch lands.

7) Handoff notes for next shift
- Watch for 'cache eviction rate' and 'persistence write latency' metrics; early warning threshold set at 250/min.
- If recurrence observed: 1) pin routing to fallback variant 2) enable additional logging for persistence writes 3) contact Lina (runtime owner) + infra on-call.
- Slack playbook channel: #sre-ops (thread id attached in linked_artifacts).

8) Misc items and housekeeping
- Quick doc: local commands used during mitigation appended to PR (INFRA-618) for reproducibility.
- Post-incident blameless retro scheduled: 2027-08-29 16:00 UTC (calendar: ops-retrospectives).
- Notes to include in retro: why canary promoted gptx-v1-q, telemetry gaps (persistence I/O), alert tuning.

9) Personal notes / observations (informal)
- Logged an intermittent 'spawn-worker-fail' trace during mitigation—might be unrelated but left trace in logs for follow-up (ticket SRE-4330).
- Consider adding small synthetic that exercises persistence-enabled models overnight to catch I/O regressions sooner.

End of watch: leaving monitoring on. Please escalate to SRE lead if anything spikes overnight. Thanks—Asha
